html:
The civic-military dictatorship ruled Uruguay from 27 June 1973, when President Juan María Bordaberry dissolved parliament with the army's backing, until civilian rule returned in March 1985.

In the 1960s the economy stalled, and the urban guerrillas of the Tupamaros robbed banks and kidnapped officials. The army crushed them by 1972 and then took power. It banned parties and unions, and jailed tens of thousands; for a time Uruguay had the highest share of political prisoners in the world. Many were tortured, and some were killed or disappeared, at home and in Argentina under Operation Condor.

About one in ten Uruguayans left the country. In 1980 voters rejected a constitution written by the military, and talks led to elections in 1984. Among the prisoners released was the Tupamaro José Mujica. Writers such as Eduardo Galeano went into exile.
sum: The civic-military dictatorship ruled Uruguay from 27 June 1973, when President Juan María Bordaberry dissolved parliament with the army's backing, until civilian rule returned in March 1985.
